Matched RecHarness Amazon task: four datasets Movies_and_TV,
Industrial_and_Scientific, Electronics, CDs_and_Vinyl, macro-average validation
HR@10. Start from RecHarness sasrec_perdataset. Preprocessing seed=0 and training
seed=42, exactly as run2.sh. The host executes your train.py and then independently
evaluates working/predict.py using the pinned RecHarness benchmark (200 validation
users/category, 99 unique negative candidates, evaluation seed=42). Test labels and
test metrics are unavailable during search. Retain all four categories and dataset
routing. DATA_DIR must remain os.environ['GAGC_DATA_DIR']; write artifacts beneath
your trial directory, as the baseline does. Training may change model architecture,
loss, optimizer, sampling and hyperparameters, as in RecHarness. Do not alter input
splits, invent metrics, read hidden test files, fetch extra datasets/pretrained weights,
or change the host evaluator. Changes to inference must also update the predictor
writer so working/predict.py loads the trained architecture. Keep execution single-GPU;
the host provides four concurrent trial slots and 64 CPU cores. No shell actions,
filesystem inspection, or training tools are needed in the LLM call: return code.
All training, diagnostics, debugging and failed trials consume the method's shared
43,200 GPU-second search budget. LLM time and final held-out inference are recorded
separately, matching run2.sh's separate final-evaluation step.
The original RecHarness tools layer sets SASREC_EPOCHS=200 (overriding the template's
standalone default of 300); this same environment default applies here.

METHOD: self_evolverec

Diagnostic task adapter: diagnosis_tools.py must retain class DiagnosisProbe(view, device)
and method run_full_diagnosis(train_loader), returning metrics and metric_definitions.
view.model is the actual trained nn.Module. view.item_emb, log2feats(sequence),
predict_score(features, items), user_train, meta_data, review_data implement the
initial SASRec compatibility contract. Adapt probes when changing the architecture.
train_loader yields (None, sequence, positive, negative), tensors of shape B x L.
Only public interaction histories, item titles, descriptions and timestamps are available.
Review ratings/text, item ratings/categories/prices/stores are NOT available in this
shared RecHarness task. Never invent them. Simulator diversity/conformity traits are
explicitly unobserved. Twenty real training users (five/category) receive full-catalog
unseen-item recommendations, as the native simulator requires. Selection uses the
common macro validation HR@10, replacing the native HR@5/NDCG@5 combined score.

NATIVE ROLE: Reflection Agent

You are an expert research assistant. You will receive a research report (in Markdown) and a newly proposed idea for that report's research problem. Your job is to identify any gaps or issues—such as missing details, logical flaws, or questionable evaluations of novelty, impact, or implementation difficulty.  

- If the report and idea contain all necessary information, do not generate any follow-up questions.  
- If you detect a knowledge gap or something that needs deeper exploration, generate one or more self-contained follow-up queries. Each query must include enough context so that a web search could answer it, For each query, give a short note explaining why you use the query and what you hope it will reveal.
- Focus on technical details, implementation specifics, and any emerging methods or references that were overlooked.  
- Use clear, direct language and avoid unnecessary jargon.

 ## Search results
Closest history-only approaches: [ICSRec (WSDM 2024)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2310.14318) creates subsequences with a dynamic sliding operation, aligns subsequences sharing a next-item target, and learns clustered intent prototypes through contrastive objectives. It includes SASRec comparisons and component ablations on Amazon Beauty/Sports/Toys plus MovieLens, using full-catalog ranking; reported gains therefore do not directly predict this benchmark’s sampled HR@10. [IOCLRec (AAAI 2025)](https://ojs.aaai.org/index.php/AAAI/article/view/33390) similarly segments histories into coarse intent subsequences and applies three contrastive modules. These support latent-intent learning from interactions, but segmentation does not establish that a real purchase purpose changed or was satisfied.

For multiple timescales, [ScaleRec (2026)](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0306457325002596) combines variable-length patches, intra-patch local attention, inter-patch attention, and adaptive filtering of redundant interactions. [HM4SR (WWW 2025)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2501.14269) combines interactive and temporal mixtures of experts with explicit timestamp embeddings. Its multimodal inputs and category-prediction auxiliary task make the complete method unsuitable for the available data, though temporal routing is transferable. The simpler [TiSASRec](https://github.com/JiachengLi1995/TiSASRec) provides an established SASRec extension using relative time intervals alongside absolute positions.

Practical synthesis, rather than a published result: retain causal SASRec and add a small gated mixture of recent-suffix, timestamp-decayed, and long-history representations. Condition gating on observed gaps and representation changes; treat any change-point interpretation as a hypothesis. Ablate each component against SASRec and the transition residual, inspect short-history performance, and select using the common four-category validation macro HR@10. The reviewed evidence does not establish gains on these exact categories or justify suppressing supposedly satisfied needs.

---

Recent work supports combining global transitions with learned relationship structure, but complementarity should not be equated with textual similarity. [SComGNN (2024)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2401.02130) models complementary relationships through both relevance and dissimilarity, using low-pass and mid-pass graph filters. [Revisiting Graph Projections (2025)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2506.09209) infers complementary relationships using directed weighted projections of user–item interactions. These motivate asymmetric source/target representations rather than symmetric text-similarity edges; neither establishes that every observed sequential transition represents functional compatibility.

Uncertainty modeling offers a separate mechanism for controlling unreliable graph signals. [DGLSR (2025)](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.ipm.2025.104119) represents graph nodes with Gaussian means and covariances to capture uncertain transition relationships. [UFRec (2026 preprint)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.28493) weights multi-step future supervision according to next-item confidence, with auxiliary components used only during training. These support adaptive confidence weighting, but do not directly validate distinct-user edge-support gating.

A plausible synthesis—not an established result—is a shared asymmetric successor scorer combining collaborative item embeddings with title/description token features learned from scratch. Shared parameters could score previously unobserved edges between known items; distinct-user transition counts, shrinkage, and predictive uncertainty could gate an empirical edge residual. Validate these components separately. The no-pretraining constraint matters: [the 2025 comparative study of inductive recommenders](https://doi.org/10.1007/s10618-025-01134-2) uses Sentence-BERT textual features, so its findings do not establish equivalent performance for locally learned text encoders. Compatibility remains a hypothesis learned from permitted histories and text.

---

Evidence supports testing the objective before replacing SASRec. [gSASRec’s 2024 summary](https://www.ijcai.org/proceedings/2024/0939.pdf) attributes much of SASRec’s disadvantage against BERT4Rec to negative-sampling-induced overconfidence; controlling sampling substantially closes the gap. It recommends gBCE with calibration t=0.75 and 128–256 negatives, subject to compute limits. For RecHarness, a useful controlled comparison is unchanged SASRec with baseline BCE, multi-negative gBCE, and uniform sampled-softmax cross-entropy. Training margins alone cannot select among them.

Sampling correction depends on the objective and actual proposal distribution. [Correcting the LogQ Correction (RecSys 2025)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2507.09331) identifies a flaw in conventional correction: the positive is always included, whereas negatives are sampled. Its refined formulation accounts for that distinction and improves over standard correction. In-batch negatives offer efficient candidate reuse but follow item popularity; uniform evaluation candidates do not make in-batch training uniform. A [2024 sequential-recommendation comparison](https://arxiv.org/abs/2410.17276) finds substantial dataset-dependent accuracy and popularity tradeoffs across random, popularity, mixed, and adaptive sampling.

Aggressive hard mining risks penalizing unobserved positives. [UFNRec](https://arxiv.org/abs/2208.04116), an earlier relevant method, uses teacher soft labels and consistency regularization for suspected false negatives. Practical experiment proposal: first establish uniform multi-negative performance, then test a small semi-hard mixture excluding known training positives; treat false-negative identification as uncertain.
